title: Silicon & Sepia - The Corkboard Pin Wall

affordance_translation.physical_behavior: A corkboard wall: photos and notes pinned at arbitrary angles; you step back to see the whole board and lean in to read one note; a compass helps you orient.
affordance_translation.digital_mechanic: An infinite pannable/zoomable canvas of pinned photos with rotation and overlap; one unified gesture system (mouse, touch, trackpad pinch, momentum); a radar minimap keeps orientation; an auto-placement algorithm packs new photos without overlapping curated ones.

design_tokens.borders: Photo prints with white frames; push-pin heads as the only circular chrome; torn-note edges on labels
design_tokens.elevation: Board-flat base with pinned items casting small directional shadows; zoom creates genuine scale depth
design_tokens.typography: Handwritten and typewriter labels pinned next to photos; map legend in small caps

interactive_mechanics: Pan/zoom the wall with momentum across all input device types
Radar minimap shows current viewport within the whole board
Pin/pack new photos via auto-placement without overlap; drag to re-pin
usability_notes: Corkboard suits galleries of memory-like content (photos, milestones). The infinite canvas is powerful but disorienting: the minimap and a 'reset view' affordance are mandatory; keyboard users need a list alternative to spatial navigation. Performance: viewport-cull pinned items. Source: Devpost project documentation (self-reported mechanics).
